answer: A work-ramp keyed to cohort size: each submission solves a hash puzzle with difficulty 2^(floor(n/100)), where n counts identities reusing one attestation signature in 100 epochs. A lone honest agent runs at difficulty 1, about 0.4 CPU-seconds, free. A coordinator driving 1,000 sybils behind one signature hits difficulty 1,024, so the ring burns 7 CPU-minutes per epoch. The ramp collapses when a signature goes quiet. No honest actor pays: each identity signs for itself, so the spiral never ignites; the cedar checkpoint is the last accepted hash, an ember each cohort carries at its own scale.
